subject: Phased commit and term discount — SilverLeaf proposal
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@silverleaftx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Phased commit and term discount — SilverLeaf proposal

Hi Oliver,

Thanks again for a productive demo yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a tailored proposal for a 3-year committed prepay with a phased payment schedule to match SilverLeaf's internal budgeting cycles. Top-line: $2.4M total commitment over 36 months. Proposed cadence: Year 1: $500k (initial), Year 2: $950k, Year 3: $950k.

We're proposing a 24% term discount on list pricing for a full 3-year prepay. Key items:
- Dedicated support and priority capacity allocation for the term
- Quarterly business reviews and a runway credit for model upgrades
- 45 day implementation timeline once signed

I've attached the term sheet (SilverLeaf_Redline_v2.pdf) and a phased-commit schedule (Phased_Commit_Schedule.xlsx). Please review and let me know if you'd like to walk through the numbers together — happy to set up a quick call.

Best,
Tessa
--
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0127

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@silverleaftx.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Phased commit and term discount — SilverLeaf proposal

Tessa —

Thanks for the proposal and the quick turnaround. The structure looks close to what we need, but two asks from our side before we can move to signature: 1) we need a deeper term discount — the CFO is pushing for ~32% given the size of the commitment, and 2) we need more frontloaded credits in Year 1 to support a heavy ramp of pilots across three business units (they want ~75% of the first-year consumption available as credits).

If Redwood can meet on either of those, we can accelerate to an approved PO within two weeks.

Oliver
Oliver Grant
VP Finance (interim)
SilverLeaf Therapeutics
oliver.grant@silverleaftx.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@silverleaftx.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SilverLeaf asks — need exec guidance

Team — forwarding Oliver's reply. They are asking for 32% term and ~75% frontloaded Y1 credits. Current guideline: discount cap for this tier is 22% without Director signoff. We are already at 24% in the proposal.

Questions:
- Is there room to stretch to 28% with added conditions (e.g., no early termination credits, stricter usage baselines)?
- Can we accommodate a higher Y1 frontload but balance it with a true-up at the end of Year 1 based on consumption?

Karthik, can you run the numbers vs. projected utilization and show incremental downside on the unit economics?
Marissa / Vivek — need guidance if this is an exec-level concession or a firm no.

Thanks,
Tessa

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SilverLeaf asks — need exec guidance

Tessa —

I ran the headcount and utilization scenarios with Karthik. Summary:
- Stretching to 32% materially increases payback beyond our standard commit models and would require a material uplift in guaranteed minimums to be acceptable.
- We can entertain 28% as a one-time executive concession if we get: 1) a binding minimum consumption schedule (true-up at end of Y1), 2) prepayment for Year 1 at 60% (not 75%), and 3) a clause that reduces priority allocation if they fall >30% below forecast in any rolling quarter.

If Vivek is comfortable with the 28% cap and the three conditions above, I recommend pushing that forward to Finance + Legal for rapid redline.

-Marissa
VP, Commercial Deals
Redwood Inference

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SilverLeaf asks — need exec guidance

Thanks team — appreciate the quick analysis. I agree with Marissa's fallback path. Approve escalation to Finance + Legal on the basis of a one-time 28% term discount provided the following are included in the redline:
- Year 1 prepay at 60% (no more than 60% frontload)
- A consumption true-up at 12 months with a clear formula and recovery mechanism
- A rollback clause for priority capacity if utilization < 70% of forecast for two consecutive quarters

Legal: ensure limitation of liability and no open-ended SLA credits in the event of non-performance. Finance: model the downside and include clear milestone-triggered payment schedule in the SOW.

Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@silverleaftx.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T17:34:00-07:00
Subject: Approved: SilverLeaf one-time concession (terms to be redlined)

Oliver / Team —

We appreciate SilverLeaf's strategic interest in a multi-year partnership. I have approved a one-time executive concession of a 28% term discount on the $2.4M 3-year prepay, subject to the following (these will be reflected in the redline and the DocuSign envelope):
1) Year 1 prepayment capped at 60% of the total first-year value (no 75% frontload)
2) Twelve-month consumption true-up with repayment terms for any shortfall (90 day recovery window)
3) Priority allocation rollback clause if utilization is more than 30% below forecast for two consecutive quarters
4) No SLA credit exposure beyond defined remediation in the contract; Legal to keep liability carve-outs intact

We will send an updated redline (SilverLeaf_Redline_v2.pdf) to you and a DocuSign link for signature. Once countersigned, Redwood will initiate onboarding and reserve the requested capacity.

Next steps for Tessa: pass the updated redline to Oliver and coordinate with Legal/Finance for the DocuSign envelope.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference
